**Observations:**
- **Untouched pixels.** Row 0 (inputs 0–27) carries only tiny weights, all with |w| ≤ ~0.036. That matches a uniform initialisation with bound 1/√784 ≈ 0.036, so these pixels were essentially never non-zero during training.
- **Very top of the frame is used.** From row 1 onward, weights grow well beyond that initial range. Row 1 already has learned weights of about 0.1–0.3 across columns ~4–23. Row 2 has large weights across most of its width, with one of about 0.31.
- **Left and right edges are used.** Throughout the image there are recurring large-magnitude weights (|w| ≈ 0.2–0.38) at the extreme left and right columns, roughly columns 0–2 and 25–27. The pixels nearest the border carry some of the strongest weights in the matrix, often with the same sign across many hidden units.
- **The bottom rows are used.** Rows 25–27 have learned weights of up to about ±0.3.
- **Hidden units look like broad region detectors, not thin strokes.** Many units have smooth regional sign patterns: large vertical bands at the left versus right of the image, top-versus-bottom contrasts, and a wide central blob. They do not look like localised pen-stroke detectors.
- **Output layer.** W2 is dense, and each class mixes many hidden units with weights of ±0.5–1.3. No single obvious detector maps to one class.

**Reasoning:**
- The format (28×28 grayscale, 10 classes, MLP) fits MNIST-style datasets: MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, or an EMNIST digits subset.
- In MNIST and EMNIST digits, the strokes are size-normalised into a centred 20×20 box. The outer ~2–4 pixels in every direction are almost always zero, so their weights would stay near initialisation. Here the border columns and the first and last rows have strongly trained weights, which argues against MNIST.
- KMNIST characters are also roughly centred and stroke-like, which again leaves the edges mostly empty.
- Fashion-MNIST objects often fill the whole frame: trousers, coats and pullovers span the full height, bags and sandals span the full width. Its silhouettes are filled regions, which fits the broad, blob- and band-shaped receptive fields and the strong use of edge columns.

**Dataset:** Fashion-MNIST (Zalando article images, 28×28 grayscale).

**Classes:** 0 T-shirt/top, 1 Trouser, 2 Pullover, 3 Dress, 4 Coat, 5 Sandal, 6 Shirt, 7 Sneaker, 8 Bag, 9 Ankle boot.

**Confidence:** 68%
